subject: psychology
title: Issues & Debates: Bias in Psychology
welcome_lead: Whose psychology? Gender and culture shape what gets studied.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology issues: gender bias alpha beta, culture bias ethnocentrism emic etic.
final_note: Spot the bias before you accept the finding.

concepts.def: Exaggerating differences between men and women.
Minimising real differences between men and women.
Male as norm — female behaviour seen as abnormal.
Judging other cultures by one's own standards.
Studying behaviour from inside a culture.
Studying behaviour from outside, claiming universals.

walkthroughs.body_html: Alpha bias exaggerates: Freud's belief that women have weaker superegos. Beta bias ignores: stress research (Taylor 2000) was done on men but generalised to women. Androcentrism follows beta bias — the male norm becomes the standard against which women are 'deviant'.

Strange Situation (Ainsworth 1978) was designed in the US and applied worldwide — but Japanese infants rarely separate from mothers, so they appear 'insecure-resistant' at high rates. Imposed etic: using a tool designed in one culture as if it were universal.

Cultural relativism: behaviour can only be judged in cultural context. Emic approaches work inside a culture; etic compare across. Berry (1969) called for emic-derived measures combined into a 'derived etic'.
